A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Transformer Copilot study. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices support comparison, including matching material relocated in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original reasoning and recommendation experiments, efficiency measurements, transferability tests and ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains those original empirical results and adds pooling-method and loss-function comparisons in Tables 19–20.

M1.justification: The Mistake Log inputs, Copilot architecture, mean pooling, RMSE objective, joint training and inference correction remain unchanged. The added explanations and ablations evaluate existing design choices without replacing the proposed method.

E1.justification: Both versions retain Commonsense170K and Math10K training coverage and the same 12 evaluation benchmarks. The new ablations reuse PIQA, AQuA and GSM8K; transferability experiments are relocated rather than newly introduced.

E2.justification: Tables 19–20 add max/sum pooling and cross-entropy/KL-divergence variants as evaluated comparators for the proposed component choices. The established benchmark baseline sets, including LLaMA/Mistral-Pro, MergeKit and TIES, remain unchanged.

E3.justification: v2 adds pooling comparisons using LLaMA-3.1-8B plus T-Copilot-1B on GSM8K/AQuA, and loss comparisons using Qwen2.5-7B plus T-Copilot-3B on PIQA/AQuA. Existing splits, metrics, training budgets and hyperparameter tables are unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix F.4 adds two focused ablations testing mean pooling against max/sum pooling and RMSE against cross-entropy/KL divergence. Earlier checkpoint, attention-insertion and correction-strength ablations, along with token-level case studies, are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report averages over three random-seed runs. The new checklist repeats this practice without adding uncertainty estimates or significance tests; existing graphical uncertainty displays are unchanged.

E6.justification: Earlier numerical results are retained. Table 19 newly reports GSM8K accuracy of 63.2/65.8 for max/sum pooling versus the retained mean-pooling score of 66.1. Table 20 adds PIQA scores of 88.1/90.4 for cross-entropy/KL versus the retained RMSE score of 92.5.

T1.justification: The proof moves from Appendix C to B and is corrected: v2 explicitly requires 0 <= lambda <= 1 for the inequality step and defines lambda_0 as the minimum of 1 and the previous bound. The theorem's existence claim and remaining derivation are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same architectural, training and inference contributions, performance improvement up to 34.5%, and efficiency, scalability and transferability claims.

C2.justification: New Appendix A.4 explains why predicting probability discrepancies is a regression task and why converting the target for cross-entropy/KL could lose information. Appendix F.4 adds interpretations supporting pooling and loss choices. The limitations discussion is moved unchanged.

D1.justification: v1 promises a future code release; v2 presents a direct Code link and states in its checklist that implementation accompanies the manuscript. Repository availability cannot be verified from the PDFs. The 128-round CPU buffer and memory figures were already documented in v1.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to TATTOO, ReasonFlux-PRM, Demystifying Reinforcement Learning in Agentic Reasoning, and Defending Against Indirect Prompt Injection by Instruction Detection. It removes the reasoning survey and STEM-pom references. The substantive positioning against fine-tuning, self-refinement, boosting and neural exploration remains stable.

P1.justification: Transferability and scalability move into Section 5.2; buffer details move earlier and limitations move to Appendix H. v2 adds the loss rationale, acknowledgments and NeurIPS checklist, and updates author/contact information. Most existing prose remains unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 adds the two small ablation tables and relocates v1's transferability Table 14 and scaling Figure 7 into the main text as Table 3 and Figure 6. Existing scientific graphics and table structures are otherwise retained, with localized layout adjustments.

improvement.justification: v2 corrects an omitted condition in the proof and supplies direct empirical support and clearer reasoning for existing pooling and loss choices. Moving transferability and scaling evidence into the main text also improves accessibility. These are useful, limited gains: the core evidence is unchanged and the new ablations remain narrow without uncertainty estimates.
